papers.title: Sample, Align, Synthesize: Graph-Based Response Synthesis with ConGrs
papers.authors: S. Ghosh, S.S. Warraich, D. Tarsadiya, G. Yauney, S. Swayamdipta
papers.description: Introduced Consensus Graphs (ConGrs), a flexible DAG-based data structure that captures shared information and semantic variation across multiple sampled LM responses to the same prompt, enabling task-dependent decoding into a single, more reliable response.
highlights: Designed **Consensus Graphs (ConGrs)**, built using a lightweight lexical sequence alignment algorithm from bioinformatics, supplemented by targeted use of a secondary LM judge
Designed task-dependent decoding methods to synthesize a single, final response from the ConGr data structure
Improved factual precision on two long-form biography generation tasks by up to **31%** over an average sampled response, while reducing reliance on LM judges by **more than 80%**
Increased appropriate abstention rate by up to **56%** across three refusal-based tasks requiring abstention on unanswerable queries
Improved accuracy on the MATH and AIME reasoning tasks by up to **6 points** over self-verification and majority-vote baselines

papers.title: How Reliable is Language Model Micro-Benchmarking?
papers.authors: G. Yauney, S.S. Warraich, S. Swayamdipta
papers.description: Introduced a meta-evaluation measure for LLM micro-benchmarking that quantifies how reliably a micro-benchmark can rank two models as a function of their performance gap on the full benchmark, revealing when small evaluation subsets fail to preserve model rankings.
highlights: Proposed a **meta-evaluation measure** for micro-benchmarking that analyzes ranking reliability as a function of the performance difference between model pairs on the full benchmark

Found that no micro-benchmarking method can consistently rank model pairs **3.5 points apart on MMLU-Pro** or **4 points apart on BIG-Bench Hard**, contrary to prior work suggesting as few as 10 examples suffice

Showed that reliably ranking model pairs with similar performance often requires as many as **250 examples**, at which point random sampling becomes competitive with existing micro-benchmarking methods
Found that on 25-example MMLU-Pro micro-benchmarks comparing 8B instruction-tuned models, **more than half** of pairwise comparisons are not likely to be preserved

papers.title: Residual Balanced Attention Network for Real-Time Traffic Scene Semantic Segmentation
papers.authors: A. Kherraki, S.S. Warraich, M. Maqbool, R. El Ouazzani
papers.description: Proposed RBANet, a robust and lightweight CNN for real-time traffic scene semantic segmentation, introducing a novel balanced attention module and a novel residual module to jointly optimize precision and computational efficiency for intelligent transportation systems.
highlights: Designed **RBANet**, a lightweight CNN combining a novel **balanced attention module** and a novel **residual module** for real-time traffic scene semantic segmentation
Achieved strong precision using only **0.74M parameters**, benchmarking three loss functions to identify the best-performing combination
Evaluated on **CamVid**, the most widely used semantic segmentation dataset, outperforming related work on the precision-efficiency tradeoff

items.title: ConGrs: Graph-Based Response Synthesis for Factual LLM Generation
items.description: Consensus Graphs (ConGrs): a DAG-based data structure that synthesizes epistemic signals across multiple sampled LM responses into a single, more reliable response. Accepted to COLM 2026.
items.problem: Sampling a language model multiple times exposes rich information about its response distribution, but existing methods can't efficiently synthesize that variation across long-form responses into a single, more reliable answer.
approach: Built Consensus Graphs (ConGrs), a flexible DAG-based structure representing shared information and semantic variation across sampled LM responses to the same prompt
Constructed ConGrs with a lightweight lexical sequence alignment algorithm from bioinformatics, supplemented by targeted use of a secondary LM judge
Designed task-dependent decoding methods to synthesize a single, final response from the ConGr structure
impact: Up to 31% improvement in factual precision on two biography generation tasks over an average response
Reduced reliance on LM judges by more than 80% compared to other methods
Increased abstention rate by up to 56% on refusal-based tasks, and improved MATH/AIME reasoning accuracy by up to 6 points
items.role: Researcher, under Dr. Swabha Swayamdipta, USC

items.title: Reliable Micro-Benchmarking for LLM Evaluation
items.description: A meta-evaluation measure for LLM micro-benchmarking that reveals when small evaluation subsets fail to reliably preserve model rankings from full benchmarks. ICLR 2026 Oral.
items.problem: Micro-benchmarking promises cheaper LLM evaluation by testing on small subsets of full benchmarks, but it wasn't clear whether these subsets can rank models as consistently as the full benchmarks they replace, or more consistently than a random sample.
approach: Introduced a meta-evaluation measure investigating how reliably a micro-benchmark ranks two models as a function of their performance difference on the full benchmark
Evaluated existing micro-benchmarking methods, including TinyBenchmarks' P-IRT and GP-IRT, against random sampling on MMLU-Pro and BIG-Bench Hard
Quantified the trade-off between micro-benchmark size and ranking reliability across model-pair performance gaps
impact: No micro-benchmarking method reliably ranks model pairs 3.5 points apart on MMLU-Pro or 4 points apart on BIG-Bench Hard
Reliable ranking of closely-performing models often requires up to 250 examples, at which point random sampling becomes competitive
More than half of pairwise comparisons are not preserved on 25-example MMLU-Pro micro-benchmarks of 8B instruction-tuned models
Accepted to ICLR 2026 as an Oral presentation
